name: Sistine Chapel ceiling
info: The Sistine Chapel ceiling is the fresco cycle Michelangelo painted in the papal chapel in the Vatican between 1508 and 1512 for Pope Julius II, with nine scenes from Genesis at its centre and over 300 figures in all.

facts.made: Painted by Michelangelo, a sculptor by training, at the commission of Pope Julius II, with theological advice that is debated and scaffolding built by Piero Roselli
facts.form: A fresco on a shallow barrel vault about 35 metres long and 14 metres wide, with a painted architectural frame, nine central scenes from Genesis, twelve prophets and sibyls, ancestors of Christ and four corner scenes
facts.where: The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, the papal chapel built within the Vatican between 1477 and 1480 by Pope Sixtus IV
facts.known: the Creation of Adam; nine scenes from the Book of Genesis; the nude ignudi; seven prophets and five sibyls; the ancestors of Christ in the lunettes; the restoration of 1980 to 1994; the setting for papal conclaves

t: Michelangelo painted the ceiling between 1508 and 1512 for Pope Julius II. He was a sculptor who first suggested that Raphael should take the work, and he had been promised 3,000 ducats.

Julius II proposed twelve Apostles in the spandrels; Michelangelo negotiated a grander scheme with nine scenes from Genesis, prophets, sibyls and ancestors of Christ, and the finished work has over 300 figures.
Candle smoke and varnish dimmed the colours over the centuries; a restoration from 1980 to 1994 revealed brighter colours and drew both praise and criticism.
dyk: According to Vasari and Condivi, Michelangelo painted standing, not lying on his back as the biographer Paolo Giovio imagined, and the final narrative scene, God in the act of creation, was painted in a single day.
ev: A diagonal crack left the chapel unusable for six months, and Julius II had the damaged starry ceiling removed
Michelangelo signed the contract on 8 May for a fee of 3,000 ducats
The first half of the ceiling was shown, with a preliminary viewing and an official one the next day
The finished ceiling was revealed on All Hallows' Eve and shown to the public the next day
A gunpowder explosion in the Castel Sant'Angelo damaged part of the Flood fresco and one of the ignudi
A restoration began with the lunettes, after preliminary tests in 1979
Pope John Paul II unveiled the restored ceiling

sections.origins:
The Sistine Chapel is the large papal chapel built within the Vatican between 1477 and 1480 by Pope Sixtus IV, for whom it is named. Its walls had been decorated about twenty years before Michelangelo's work. The middle level holds frescoes of the Life of Christ on the right side and the Life of Moses on the left, painted by Sandro Botticelli, Domenico Ghirlandaio, Pietro Perugino, Pinturicchio, Luca Signorelli and Cosimo Rosselli, while the upper level has the windows and, between them, painted niches with the first 32 popes. The original ceiling, by Pier Matteo d'Amelia, showed stars over a blue background, like the Arena Chapel at Padua decorated by Giotto.

For six months in 1504 a diagonal crack in the vault made the chapel unusable, and Pope Julius II (Giuliano della Rovere) had the damaged painting removed by Piero Roselli, a friend of Michelangelo. Julius II was a "warrior pope" who campaigned to unite and empower Italy under the leadership of the Church and who invested in symbols of his temporal power, among them the rebuilding of St. Peter's Basilica. He summoned Michelangelo to Rome in early 1505 to design his tomb. In 1506, the year the foundation stone of the new St. Peter's was laid, he conceived a programme to paint the ceiling.
sections.content:
The ceiling is a shallow barrel vault around 35 metres long and 14 metres broad, cut by the chapel's windows into a row of lunettes alternating with spandrels. A fictive architectural cornice delineates the central, almost flat field, which five pairs of painted ribs divide into four large rectangles and five smaller ones. These appear open to the sky and hold nine scenes from the Book of Genesis in three groups of three: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the creation of Adam and Eve and their expulsion from the Garden of Eden, and the plight of humanity and of the family of Noah. Around the five smaller scenes sit twenty nude male youths, the ignudi, who flank ten medallions; their precise significance is unknown.

Below the cornice are seven prophets of Israel and five sibyls of the Graeco-Roman world, painted in the spandrels above the windows and notable in Christian tradition for foretelling the Messiah or the Nativity. Above the windows the lunettes carry tablets naming the ancestors of Christ with accompanying figures. In the four corners the doubled spandrels show the Brazen Serpent, the Punishment of Haman, Judith and Holofernes, and David and Goliath, stories of the salvation of Israel.
sections.making:
Michelangelo, who was not primarily a painter but a sculptor, was reluctant to take on the work and suggested his young rival Raphael instead. According to Giorgio Vasari, Julius II was provoked by Bramante to insist. The contract was signed on 8 May 1508 for a fee of 3,000 ducats. Bramante built the first scaffolding, hung by ropes from holes in the ceiling; Michelangelo disliked it because he would have had to paint around the holes, and Piero Roselli built a freestanding scaffold instead. Michelangelo could find no assistants well-versed enough in fresco and decided to paint the whole ceiling alone.

The pope's scheme, which has not survived, called for twelve Apostles in the spandrels within an interlocking pattern of squares and circles. Michelangelo found it left too few human figures and, in his own later words, was permitted "to do as I liked", a claim many art historians suspect is overstated. The plaster began to grow mould because it was too wet, and Giuliano da Sangallo explained how to remove it. A new area of plaster, a giornata, was laid each day. The work began at the west end and moved towards the altar, and Michelangelo's style broadened as the scale of the figures grew. Scholars debate the order of painting and the arrangement of the scaffold: the majority view is a sequence of phases, with the scaffold moved each time, while Ulrich Pfisterer argues that it spanned the whole chapel for years at a time.
sections.reception:
After the first half was shown on 14 August 1511 and the whole on 31 October 1512, Vasari wrote that people from everywhere rushed to see it and were left amazed and speechless. At the age of 37 Michelangelo was called il divino, and he was regarded thereafter as the greatest artist of his time. The ceiling was immediately considered one of the greatest masterpieces of all time, a view that continues. Not every response was admiring: a number of critics, including Pope Adrian VI, were angered by the nudity of the ignudi.

Interpretations differ. The overt subject is the Christian doctrine of humanity's need for salvation through Jesus, and the ceiling also shows the Renaissance effort to reconcile Christian theology with humanist philosophy. Edgar Wind proposed that the ten medallions represented violations of the Ten Commandments, but John W. O'Malley notes that the infractions would then be out of order. Modern scholars have not found a written source for the theological programme and have asked whether Michelangelo devised it entirely himself. Jelbert has suggested that the ceiling is an intellectual Renaissance puzzle based on celestial imagery and the symbolic meaning of the stars.
sections.survival:
The ceiling had suffered some damage by the mid-16th century. In 1797 a gunpowder explosion in the Castel Sant'Angelo damaged part of the Flood fresco and one of the ignudi, which a drawing by a pupil of Michelangelo preserved. Over the centuries candle smoke and layers of varnish aged the paint and muted the original colours. Some restorations took place in the early and mid-20th century. The lunettes were in the worst state: of all the paintings in the chapel they were the dirtiest, and the panels nearest the windows were hard to see in daylight because of halation.

After preliminary tests in 1979, the ceiling was restored between 1980 and 1992. The work upon the lunettes ran from June 1980 to October 1984; the ceiling itself was completed on 31 December 1989, and the restorers then moved on to The Last Judgment. Pope John Paul II unveiled the restoration on 8 April 1994. It was directed by Fabrizio Mancinelli and performed by Gianluigi Colalucci, Maurizio Rossi, Pier Giorgio Bonetti and Bruno Baratti. Removing the grime revealed bright, saturated colours that suggest daytime scenes and a springlike atmosphere. Critics assert that much of Michelangelo's original work, in particular pentimenti, highlights, shadows and details painted a secco, was lost with the accretions.
sections.legacy:
The ceiling had a profound effect on other artists even before it was completed. Vasari wrote that Bramante let Raphael into the chapel in Michelangelo's absence, and that on seeing the prophets Raphael scraped off and repainted his Isaiah in Sant'Agostino in imitation of them. Raphael's Heraclitus in the School of Athens resembles Michelangelo's Jeremiah, with Michelangelo's own countenance. The poses of the ignudi were copied by Bartolommeo Bandinelli and by Raphael's workshop, and Gabriele Bartz and Eberhard König write that no image has had a more lasting effect on following generations of decorative work.

Michelangelo is considered a master of cangiante, the use of different colours to represent shading, a technique he first demonstrated in the chapel, as in the robes of Daniel. Older depictions of Creation had shown God mostly immobile and enthroned; Michelangelo shows God in full-bodied movement. After the ceiling Raphael designed tapestries (1515 to 1516) for the lowest level of the walls, and Michelangelo returned to paint The Last Judgment on the altar wall. The chapel serves as the setting for papal conclaves and other important services.

summary: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512 for Pope Julius II, with nine scenes from Genesis, prophets, sibyls and the ancestors of Christ. Smoke and varnish dimmed it, and a restoration from 1980 to 1994 revealed brighter colours and drew both praise and criticism.
references: Andrew Graham-Dixon, Michelangelo and the Sistine Chapel (Weidenfeld & Nicolson, 2008)
Loren Partridge, Michelangelo. The Sistine Chapel Ceiling, Rome (George Braziller, 1996)
Ulrich Pfisterer, The Sistine Chapel: Paradise in Rome (Getty Publications, 2018)
notes: Article's Notes, References, Bibliography and Further reading sections are empty in the saved text, so references are left empty.
Start 1508 from the contract (8 May 1508) and the lead's 'between 1508 and 1512'; the article says Michelangelo probably began plans from April 1508.
Disputed: order of painting and scaffold arrangement (Wilde's phased majority theory vs Pfisterer's whole-chapel scaffold); the article does not settle it, and both are reported.

The article gives the restoration as 1980 to 1992 in one place, 1980 to 1994 in the lead and unveiling on 8 April 1994; the text says restored 1980-1992 and unveiled 1994; the lead's 'most recently from 1980 to 1994' is used in the takeaway.

Left out: the Renaissance puzzle readings of anatomy and constellations beyond a one-line mention (Jelbert's theory, single author); the Michelangelo poem (text not saved); visitor numbers and 2007 ticketing; the quotations.
Article's Bertram quotation about Michelangelo's sexuality left out.
The puzzle reading in reception is Jelbert's alone in the article.
